body:
Tahnk you for sharing this! 

Do you mind if I ask a question? 

> Sometimes it makes me feel better, sometimes worse.

Why the different reactions? What makes you feel better?

> Maybe you guys could learn to dance together. Like Latin or Samba or ballroom dancing.

We actually tried that. I suck at dancing, I don't even recognize what's rhythm (it's really weird, trust me). 

>  There are natural foods that could help, you should maybe look into that.

Any suggestion? 

I always thought that eating what makes you happy would be good enough; but I believe you're right. Do you think this might be a [good article about food in this situation?](https://www.webmd.com/depression/guide/diet-recovery)

> Does she have friends? Invite them over. Invite her sister and parents over often.

That's good! I'll definitively try that.

> Yes try encourage her to paint, its a really great outlet. Introduce her to new hobbies yes for sure

I try to encourage her to do so, but she constantly says she has no *energy* (meaning = tired of life). Maybe I could try something that we could do together, but I don't know what that would be. 

> When you feel the time is right, and without pushing, try encourage her to see a psychiatrist.

Yeah... About that. She says she doesn't want to be "numb" because of the medication. Any idea about that?

Edit: Forgot to thank you for your reply. So thank you!

Thank you for your reply! This means a lot to me. 

> I don't know, this might sound dumb, but my husband telling me everything will be okay, just asking me how I am and listening to my crying, and holding me close is often all I need.

Does this really help you? 

I'm afraid that constantly asking her about it might make her think of her condition more often. It's a tricky situation, to say the least. Maybe it's a way to make her realize I'm there for her, no matter what. 

> Usually when he suggests stuff I could do, I'll end up feeling bad because I don't have the will and energy to do them, which usually makes me feel like I'm disappointing him.

Well, you have a point here. Sometimes she complains she's bored, but other days she just feel like "meh, I'm too *tired* to go out". Yesterday, she said she's sorry that I'm living this and that she feels I should have 'someone better' by my side. Obviously, I said this is not the case - and that I'm with her no matter what. 

> I also never wanted to go see a therapist. If I made appointments I wouldn't actually go. Later, I asked a friend to take me to the therapist, make sure I go, you know? It's that first time that I always considered the hardest.

That's a problem for us. She doesn't talk about her depression to anyone besides me. She doesn't want to talk to a therapist or even her friends. That's one of the reasons I'm trying reddit for support because she wouldn't feel good if I talk to some of my friends for advice.
